newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma educators fret over timing of casino vote.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma educators fret over timing of casino vote.

text.p: A referendum on whether to allow legalized casino gambling in Oklahoma will be held Feb 10, 1998, but that choice of date has the state's educators worried.

The gambling vote comes on the same day as annual elections for approving the millage for school funding, and school officials worry that placing the two issues on the same ballot could confuse voters and lead to the defeat of both, thereby jeopardizing the schools' financial health.
They say the situation is further complicated because the petition drive that helped place the casino issue on the ballot stressed that it will generate revenues for education.

"Having the election on the same day, therefore, could be a distraction," said Bob Mooneyham, executive director of the Oklahoma State School Boards Association. "It is not beyond the realm of possibility that voters could end up voting "no" on both issues and that will penalize education."
Under Oklahoma law, elections must be held annually to approve the millage, a tax rate applied to property with each mill representing $1 of tax assessment per $1,000 of property valuation.
Gov. Frank Keating has been urged by some education officials to separate the votes but is not persuaded Oklahomans can not distiunguish between the two issues.
Rick Buchanan, a spokesman for the governor, told Reuters that Keating chose Feb. 10 because it was the first available date for the referendum.
"There is no need to change the date because they are two separate issues," he said, adding that in any event, neither involves a tax increase to worry the voters.

"Usually, voter turnout for the millage is low," Buchanan said. "The governor is making sure to inform people that the issues are distinct and separate. Also, he himself does not support casino gambling."
Mooneyham said school officials will try to make sure there is no confusion.

"The governor's decision is final. We'll have to work harder to ensure that the voters keep the issues separate. We, of course, prefer to stay in our business of educating children instead of getting caught in politics."
Currently, Oklahoma has no casino gambling. In the state's Indian nation territory, only bingo and a pull-tab type of lottery are allowed.
If voters approve casino gambling, only four locations would have it. One each will be located in Oklahoma City and Tulsa County, and the other two in counties near the Texas and Arkansas borders.
Buchanan said if the measure is approved, the state's Indian tribes would also seek to build casinos in their territory, but the state would have no authority to regulate it.
